changes.questionText: According to the passage, which of the following is true regarding factory workers in eastern mill towns after the economic boom?

options.label: A
options.text: They strongly identified with small-business entrepreneurs and professionals.

options.label: B
options.text: Their numbers tripled because of the competition for their labor among various industrialists.

options.text: They had little if any control over their own working conditions.

answer.rationale_zh: 文章指出工厂工人被排除在财产所有者阶层之外，并在雇主面前无助，直接支持他们对工作条件缺少控制。人口增长三倍描述的是城镇人口，而非工人因争夺劳动力而增长。
texts: They had little if any control over their own working conditions.

passage.text: The post-1850 economic boom in the United States had its greatest impact on eastern mill towns, such as Lowell, Massachusetts. Formerly peaceful villages became bustling towns whose factories rose to dominate their skylines. Their populations sometimes tripled in a decade, forcing propertyless workers into overcrowded, dilapidated housing. Their economies came under the domination of industrialists who competed unfairly with one another and were contemptuous of the old ways. These industrialists had economic power and the social and political power that accompanied it; town politicians catered to their interests. Other property owners, especially small-business entrepreneurs and professionals, identified with them and applauded their successes. The factory workers inevitably found themselves alienated from property owners and helpless before their employers. Thus, economic class, social status, and power were inextricably intertwined; control over property and machinery was readily transformed into complete authority.

options.text: The private sphere is superior to the public sphere.

changes.questionText: Which of the following is a criticism the author of the passage makes of Burckhardt's work?

options.text: Burckhardt failed to conduct a detailed study of all of the works of Bruni.

options.text: Burckhardt was overly influenced by nineteenth-century assumptions about women's roles.

answer.label: E
answer.text: Burckhardt overlooked important evidence because he shared an assumption contained in that evidence.

changes.questionText: Which of the following, if true, would cast the most serious doubt on the position taken by the author of the passage regarding Burckhardt's evaluation of historical evidence?

options.text: Burckhardt's scholarly works focus almost exclusively on sixteenth-century European humanists.

options.label: B
options.text: Burckhardt had read Bruni's pedagogic works and had admired them.

options.label: C
options.text: Margaret King's work has received considerable scholarly acclaim.

options.label: D

options.label: E
options.text: Margaret King's evidence is based largely on Bruni's work, which was not representative of humanist texts.

answer.rationale_zh: 作者的解释是布克哈特因共享人文主义者的性别观而未注意布鲁尼的教育主张。若布克哈特确实读过并欣赏布鲁尼的教育著作，这会最直接动摇他因未接触相关证据而忽略它的解释。
answer.label: B
answer.text: Burckhardt had read Bruni's pedagogic works and had admired them.

passage.text: The post-1850 economic boom in the United States had its greatest impact on eastern mill towns, such as Lowell, Massachusetts. Formerly peaceful villages became bustling towns whose factories rose to dominate their skylines. Their populations sometimes tripled in a decade, forcing propertyless workers into overcrowded, dilapidated housing. Their economies came under the domination of industrialists who competed unfairly with one another and were contemptuous of the old ways. These industrialists had economic power and the social and political power that accompanied it; town politicians catered to their interests. Other property owners, especially small-business entrepreneurs and professionals, identified with them and applauded their successes. The factory workers inevitably found themselves alienated from property owners and helpless before their employers. Thus, economic class, social status, and power were inextricably intertwined; control over property and machinery was readily transformed into complete authority.
